items.title: Make Stripe checkout and webhook authority fail closed, replay bounded, and redirect safe
items.why: The webhook accepts unsigned events whenever STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET is absent, ignores Stripe's timestamp tolerance and multi-signature rotation model, compares signatures non-constantly, returns success after database failures, and does not reject non-POST requests. The checkout function also forwards caller-supplied success_url and cancel_url to Stripe without an origin contract.
evidence: supabase/functions/stripe-webhook/index.ts verifies only when WEBHOOK_SECRET is truthy; an empty secret therefore grants unsigned service-role writes.
verifyStripeSignature takes one v1 value, has no timestamp tolerance, and compares computed === signature.
Webhook upsert/update errors are logged but still return HTTP 200, preventing a truthful Stripe retry.
supabase/functions/create-checkout/index.ts sends raw success_url/cancel_url directly to Stripe.
No discovered Deno test covers create-checkout or stripe-webhook; verify:edge currently reports only five test files.
items.recipe: Extract pure Stripe boundary helpers. Require a configured webhook secret, POST plus JSON, a five-minute signed timestamp window, any matching rotated v1 signature, constant-time byte comparison, bounded event shape, checked Stripe subscription fetches, and non-2xx database failures. Canonicalize checkout return URLs to an explicit PromoGrind/local allowlist and bound attribution metadata. Add adversarial Deno tests and a release invariant that fails if the webhook ever regains optional verification.

L1.recipe: Require the webhook secret, reject non-POST requests, and allowlist checkout return origins.

L2.recipe: L1 plus timestamp tolerance, rotated v1 signatures, constant-time comparison, response/error checks, and unit tests.

L3.recipe: L2 plus a pure authority contract, adversarial replay/malformed payload tests, bounded metadata, fail-closed database/Stripe outcomes, and release-gate structural enforcement.

executionLog.note: L3 shipped: webhook ingress now requires a fresh rotating HMAC signature and configured secret, checkout redirects and metadata are bounded, provider/database failures remain retryable, and 50/50 Deno checks cover the authority helpers across 15 edge entrypoints.

items.title: Give AI Chat the same explicit, inspectable data-egress contract as Promo Advisor
items.axis: privacy / artificial intelligence / UX / token efficiency
items.why: Promo Advisor correctly keeps bankroll and active books local until an unchecked explicit opt-in. Promo Chat silently transmits both on every message, while message and history text bypass the identifier redaction contract. This is cross-feature policy drift at the exact provider boundary.
evidence: PromoChat.jsx constructs userContext from appData.bankroll and appData.done unconditionally.
PromoChat strips HTML and truncates only the newest message; email, phone, account identifiers, URL secrets, and history are not redacted.
advisorPrivacy.test.js proves the intended policy: profile context stays local by default and only named fields leave after consent.
promo-chat/index.ts accepts userContext without personalizationConsent or privacyContractVersion validation.
items.recipe: Generalize the existing privacy envelope into a shared AI-egress contract for message, bounded history, and named profile fields. Add an unchecked Chat personalization control with exact field disclosure; default to local-only; redact on both client and server; bind cache keys to the sanitized body; emit an inspectable privacy receipt; and test consent, redaction, history bounds, server revalidation, and accessible UI state.

L1.recipe: Stop automatic profile transmission and add an unchecked personalization control.

L2.recipe: L1 plus client-side message/history redaction, bounded profile fields, and receipt UI/tests.

L3.recipe: L2 plus server-side contract revalidation, cross-surface semantic ratchet, cache-safe sanitized envelopes, and desktop/mobile rendered verification.

executionLog.note: L3 shipped: unchecked named-field consent, client/server double redaction, bounded versioned history, cache-safe sanitized envelopes, and privacy receipts pass client plus Edge tests. Four real-Chromium dark/light desktop/mobile captures found and repaired a light-theme transcript defect.

items.title: Make release architecture and one-command launch status executable on the actual host
items.axis: observability / infrastructure / release architecture / agent parity
items.why: check-canon-conformance reports a green vector while CANON-045 shows a checker parse error because the required local check-release-architecture.mjs is absent. Independently, launch-status.mjs tries to spawn npm.cmd with shell:false on Windows, never starts the launch gate, and collapses the spawn error into exit code unknown.
evidence: Canonical conformance: 0 GAP but CANON-045 is rendered as ERROR: could not read pass from checker output.
scripts/check-release-architecture.mjs is absent even though CANON_MATRIX marks it local and expects JSON field pass.
node scripts/launch-status.mjs --json returned Local launch gate failed with exit code unknown before any gate output.
launch-status.mjs resolves npm to npm.cmd while keeping shell:false; package-trust.mjs already carries the correct hidden cmd.exe /d /s /c npm precedent.
items.recipe: Add a public-safe local release-architecture checker that derives stable-staging and Obelisk delegation states from PROJECT_STATUS without inventing external proof, outputs the canonical pass field, and distinguishes FORGE-compatible posture from release readiness. Refactor launch-status through a tested cross-platform command spec, preserve direct child exit/error evidence, and add a fast dependency-injected regression so Windows spawn failures cannot masquerade as executed gates.

L1.recipe: Fix the Windows npm command and surface spawn errors; add the missing JSON checker.

L2.recipe: L1 plus pure command/architecture contracts and behavioral tests for local versus stable staging and hybrid identity.

L3.recipe: L2 plus deterministic receipts, conformance replay, release-surface integration, and contradiction tests spanning status, launch proofs, and public identity metadata.

executionLog.note: L3 repo-owned scope shipped: cross-platform npm transport executes on Windows, spawn failures retain exact evidence, and a public-safe CANON-007/045 checker derives honest FORGE gaps. Release tests pass. Canonical replay exposed an upstream boolean passIf parser defect; routed by signed Ark 01JV4I9IFP40116777CEC498FA without editing Studio Ops.

items.title: Replace categorical legal answers with jurisdiction-bound guidance the claim scanner can actually detect
items.axis: public trust / UX / legal claims / feedback
items.why: KnowledgeBase still answers Is this legal in my state? with Yes and states that matched betting and promo conversion are legal where online betting is legal. The 22-rule claim scanner reports zero findings because its categorical rule recognizes only two narrower question phrasings.
evidence: src/components/KnowledgeBase.jsx contains the categorical answer and a second blanket legality statement.
npm run test:public-claims passes and check-public-claims.mjs reports ok=true across 321 files.
The structural rule matches only Is PromoGrind legal or Do we need a gambling licence, so the live phrasing bypasses it.
items.recipe: Rewrite the knowledge surface around product behavior, jurisdiction/terms variability, and non-legal-advice boundaries. Expand the document rule to cover first-person and activity-level legality questions without flagging safe uncertainty text; add adversarial React/HTML fixtures and verify the content-addressed public-claims receipt changes only after the source is clean.

L2.recipe: L1 plus generalized scanner patterns and regression fixtures.

L3.recipe: L2 plus false-positive safe-negation coverage, multisurface structural fixtures, receipt replay, and visual review of the touched help surface if reachable.

executionLog.note: L3 shipped: generalized conditional-safe legal/tax claim rules surfaced 26 findings, every genuine React/static/Edge claim was rewritten around jurisdiction and qualified advice, false-positive conditions were bounded, and 24 rules now pass across 321 files with a new content hash.

items.title: Close the dynamic-import escape hatch in the Windows no-window spawn invariant
items.why: The Windows guard claims every spawn routes through safe-spawn, but render-startup-brief dynamically imports node:child_process and launches the v5 renderer without windowsHide. The guard regex detects static import/require only and therefore reports a false green.
evidence: render-startup-brief.mjs line 57 dynamically imports node:child_process and shadows the hardened spawnSync import.
The delegated spawn options omit windowsHide:true.
node scripts/check-windows-hide.mjs returns green because RAW_CP_RE has no import() branch.
items.recipe: Remove the raw dynamic import and use the already-imported hardened wrapper. Expand the sentinel and codemod to recognize static, require, and dynamic child_process acquisition, add adversarial fixtures for quote/spacing/node-prefix variants, and prove the normal plus --v5 startup paths stay hidden and preserve child exit status.

L1.recipe: Remove the dynamic import and use safe-spawn.

L2.recipe: L1 plus dynamic-import detection and regression fixtures.

L3.recipe: L2 plus codemod coverage, delegated-path behavioral proof, and a no-false-green receipt assertion.

executionLog.note: L3 shipped: startup v5 now uses the hardened spawn wrapper; the guard and codemod detect dynamic imports; 16/16 Studio script regressions and the live Windows guard pass.
